name: Magnitude
tagline: Open source inference engine for agents that tunes its kernels to your hardware
summary: Magnitude is a desktop app and CLI that runs open-weight models locally. It compiles and tunes its kernels on the user's own device before a model runs, shares prefix caches across concurrent agent sessions, and works on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD or a CPU alone. One click connects coding agents such as Pi, OpenCode, Hermes, Codex, Claude Code and Cline, and anything else can use its OpenAI-compatible API.
watching: It is a local model server built for coding agents, the same role Ollama and llama.cpp play behind the desktop's Local Llama provider, and its OpenAI-compatible API is the kind of endpoint that provider accepts.

name: rhun
tagline: Small, fast code editor written in assembly, with a terminal, Git and an agents panel
summary: rhun is a code editor for Linux, Windows and Apple Silicon Macs whose editor and pixel renderer are handwritten x86-64 assembly, translated to AArch64 at build time. It has tabs, syntax highlighting, fuzzy file and project search, an optional Vim mode and a built-in terminal. Its Git view stages, commits, pulls and pushes, shows diffs and history, and can draft commit messages with a Claude or Codex subscription or a local Ollama model. An agents panel shows Claude Code and Codex sessions as they work.
watching: It is built for the workflow where coding agents write the code and a person reads diffs, runs commands and commits, the same split the desktop's agent worktrees assume, and it watches Claude Code and Codex sessions beside the editor.
